sentences.text: The genus Telmabates contains only one currently recognized species, T. antiquus.

The species Telmabates antiquus was named and described by Howard in 1955, while a second species, T. howardae, was named by Cracraft in 1970 but was later moved to the new species Wunketru howardae by De Mendoza, Degrange, and Tambussi in 2024.
Telmabates belongs to the family Presbyornithidae.

Fossils of Telmabates were found in the Eocene Bird Clay Locality of the Sarmiento Formation in Chubut Province, Argentina, where the animal lived between 56 and 48 million years ago during the Ypresian to Lutetian stages.
